name: CT-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Bronin's large fundraising advantage over Chai
Open seat after Larson lost renomination
model.rationale: The district's D+12 lean and a favorable national environment point to a comfortable Democratic hold, and Luke Bronin has raised over $3 million with substantial outside support while Amy Chai has raised only about $21,000. Markets price the Democratic side near 96%, consistent with a Safe D rating.
model.watch: A sharp national shift toward Republicans or an unexpected Bronin scandal could narrow the margin, though a GOP win remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: John B. Larson (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Connecticut's first district is a strongly Democratic seat, and longtime incumbent John Larson will not appear on the ballot after losing renomination. Hartford mayor Luke Bronin enters the general election as the Democratic nominee with a major financial edge, having raised over $3 million and drawn significant outside spending in his favor. Republican Amy Chai has raised only about $21,000 and has minimal cash on hand.

The district's D+12 partisan lean and a favorable national environment for Democrats make a Republican upset very unlikely. Prediction markets price the Democratic side near 96%, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. The forecast is a Safe Democratic hold, with the main uncertainty being the size of the margin rather than the winner.
